question: A surgeon has to remove the very last section of a patient's small intestine. Which part is this?

options.A: Duodenum
options.B: Ileum
options.C: Jejunum
options.D: Sigmoid colon

explanation: The ileum is the final stretch of the small intestine right before it hands over food waste to the large intestine. Great job remembering that! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h2)

question: During an eye exam, what classic sign tells a doctor there is increased pressure inside the skull?

options.A: Papilledema
options.B: Cataracts
options.C: Retinal detachment
options.D: Conjunctivitis

explanation: Brilliant! Papilledema is simply the swelling of the optic nerve head. Because the optic nerve connects directly to the brain, high intracranial pressure pushes on it and shows up clearly during an eye check. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h3)

question: What happens to an infant's temperature reading if they are crying or throwing a tantrum?

options.A: It goes up because of increased facial muscle activity and blood flow
options.B: It causes the device to show an error code
options.C: It drops to a false low because of heavy breathing
options.D: It has no effect at all on infrared readings

explanation: Crying pumps up local blood circulation and muscle work around the face, which can push skin temperatures up temporarily. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the main goal of studying food, milk, and water microbiology?

options.A: Measuring the exact vitamin content in fresh farm produce
options.B: Creating new chemical preservatives for processed meals
options.C: Finding ways to completely sterilize all natural water bodies
options.D: Studying microbes that spoil consumables or cause illness

explanation: Great job! This area of microbiology focuses on finding and understanding the tiny germs that contaminate what we eat and drink, so we can prevent sickness. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of applying trauma-informed principles immediately after a community disaster?

options.A: To enforce strict behavioral rules and curfews across the neighborhood
options.B: To immediately diagnose every resident with post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: To gather clinical research data for academic publication
options.D: To build safety, de-escalate fear, and help stabilize the population

explanation: Trauma-informed disaster response prioritizes safety and trust to calm affected individuals and prevent further psychological harm. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which communication pattern involves all team members talking freely with one another without a strict central bottleneck?

options.A: Y-pattern network
options.B: All-channel network
options.C: Wheel network
options.D: Chain network

explanation: An all-channel communication network allows open, multi-directional sharing of information among all members of the group. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h4)

question: Which complication is a major risk for clients taking long-term oral NSAIDs for osteoarthritis pain?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable weight loss and high fever
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of new joint cartilage
options.C: Gastrointestinal bleeding and stomach ulcers
options.D: Permanent darkening of the skin and hair

explanation: Oral NSAIDs block protective stomach lining chemicals, putting regular users at high risk for ulcers and bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: Why is proper documentation of contraceptive counseling important in the client's health record?

options.A: It stops the client from ever changing her birth control method later
options.B: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse worked full hours
options.C: It guarantees that the healthcare facility will receive extra government funding
options.D: It ensures continuity of care and creates a legal record of the client's informed choices

explanation: Clear records allow other healthcare providers to know what method was chosen, what education was given, and what follow-up is needed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What makes probability sampling special?

options.A: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected
options.B: The researcher hand-picks individuals who fit a specific profile
options.C: Only patients with severe symptoms are included in the study
options.D: Participants are chosen based on their easy availability to the nurse

explanation: Spot on! Probability sampling uses fairness and random selection, meaning everyone in the group has a fair shot at being chosen. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which blood tests are most vital for tracking complications in a patient with severe, ongoing watery stools?

options.A: Liver enzyme panel and lipid profile
options.B: Serum electrolytes and renal function tests
options.C: Fast blood glucose and glycosylated hemoglobin
options.D: Cardiac troponin levels and clotting times

explanation: Diarrhoea washes away key electrolytes like sodium and potassium, and can stress the kidneys. Checking electrolytes and kidney function helps us catch imbalances early! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why do nurse researchers check their ideas against the FINER criteria before starting a study?

options.A: To check if the study is practical, ethical, and worth doing
options.B: To calculate the exact sample size needed for data analysis
options.C: To write the discussion section of the research paper
options.D: To select the statistical software for data entry

explanation: FINER (Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant) acts like a safety check to make sure your study idea is worth your time and safe for patients. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h4)

question: A community has non-English speakers and residents with hearing impairments. How should you adapt the emergency warning system?

options.A: Assume residents will translate the news for each other
options.B: Rely entirely on standard written flyers distributed in mailboxes
options.C: Broadcast warnings exclusively in the national official language
options.D: Provide multilingual materials and sign language interpreters

explanation: Spot on! Tailoring your messages to meet specific language and sensory needs ensures that no vulnerable group is left in the dark. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is a key nursing task during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: Approving building permits for temporary relief shelters
options.B: Directing traffic flow on major highways leading out of the disaster zone
options.C: Assessing community vulnerability and managing casualty sorting areas
options.D: Distributing military weapons to community vigilante groups

explanation: Nurses are brilliant at triage (sorting patients by urgency) and figuring out community health risks during crises. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T8#GNS315_U5_T8_h4)

question: A female patient comes to the clinic with ongoing pelvic pain, constant headaches, and severe anxiety that doctors can't quite explain. What should you keep in mind?

options.A: An adverse reaction to routine vaccination
options.B: An acute bacterial infection of the kidneys
options.C: A congenital structural defect in the pelvis
options.D: A history of physical or psychological abuse

explanation: Great thinking! Unexplained chronic aches and high anxiety can often be the body's way of showing the hidden scars of past abuse. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h3)

question: A nurse manager wants to present fall rates to bedside nurses to improve safety. How should she present it?

options.A: Emphasize the financial penalties the hospital faces from insurance
options.B: Present complex statistical regression models without explanation
options.C: Read the entire hospital policy manual out loud to the team
options.D: Focus on how shift routines and practical steps can prevent falls

explanation: Exactly! Bedside nurses love practical tips that fit into their daily ward routine and make patient care safer. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is it best to give the HPV vaccine before a person becomes sexually active?

options.A: The vaccine changes its chemical formulation based on sexual history
options.B: Adolescent immune systems cannot process the vaccine after sexual debut
options.C: The vaccine provides the highest protection before any potential exposure to the virus
options.D: Insurance policies refuse coverage for the vaccine once a person turns eighteen

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines work best when your immune system meets the pathogen before the actual virus does. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which of these is a valid medical reason to put in an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: General urinary incontinence with no skin breakdown
options.B: To make things easier for nursing staff during busy night shifts
options.C: Accurate hourly urine output measurement in a critically ill patient
options.D: The patient prefers not to get up to use the toilet at night

explanation: Spot on! We only use indwelling catheters when there is a strong medical need, like closely tracking kidney function in very sick patients. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why is a functional referral network important for big teaching hospitals?

options.A: It eliminates the need for community health nurses altogether
options.B: It guarantees that every patient gets admitted for surgery
options.C: It prevents minor health issues from clogging up specialist care
options.D: It ensures that doctors only work half-day shifts

explanation: When primary clinics handle minor cases and only refer severe ones, tertiary hospitals can focus on complex medical conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why do nurses often use non-experimental designs instead of full experiments?

options.A: Ethical or practical limits prevent manipulating certain variables
options.B: Non-experimental studies always cost more money to run
options.C: Hospital administrators ban true experiments entirely
options.D: Patients prefer answering surveys over taking medications

explanation: We can't always play scientist with people's lives! For example, it's unethical to force someone to smoke or give them a disease just to study it, so we observe what naturally happens instead. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do nursing leaders view workplace conflict as a neutral event rather than something purely bad?

options.A: Because hospital management rarely pays attention to small arguments
options.B: Because patient outcomes are never affected by staff disagreements
options.C: Because it simply signals that current dynamics need attention
options.D: Because it always leads to immediate staff resignation

explanation: Think of conflict like a warning light on a car dash. It's not automatically a disaster; it just tells you that some team dynamics need a closer look and a bit of care. [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h1)

question: How is the best way to kick off the discussion section?

options.A: By summarizing the primary findings in plain language
options.B: By proposing a brand new theory of human behavior
options.C: By listing every single p-value calculated in the study
options.D: By criticizing the work done by previous authors

explanation: Spot on! Starting with a clear, simple summary reminds your reader of the main scoop before you dive deep into what it all means. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h2)

question: You want to give mothers at a busy immunization clinic a portable guide on home care for diarrhea. What should you use?

options.A: A flannel graph
options.B: A leaflet or brochure
options.C: A radio jingle
options.D: A giant billboard

explanation: Leaflets and brochures are great because mothers can easily slip them into their bags, take them home, and check the care steps later. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is a major reason pregnant women might hide their emotional distress from healthcare providers?

options.A: Routine instructions given during antenatal classes
options.B: Complete lack of physical symptoms during gestation
options.C: The absence of hormonal fluctuations in pregnancy
options.D: Fear of being judged and stigmatized as a bad mother

explanation: So true. Stigma makes many mums keep quiet, which is why a warm, non-judgmental nursing approach is so important! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h7)

question: In an emergency, why do people in a crowd often rush back to the exact entrance they used, ignoring other exits?

options.A: Main entrances are always wider and safer during an emergency.
options.B: Security guards physically block all emergency doors.
options.C: People prefer to walk backward rather than explore new areas.
options.D: Herding behavior makes individuals follow familiar routes and mimic others.

explanation: Under stress, human nature kicks in: we tend to stick to what is familiar and copy whatever the person right next to us is doing. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h2)

question: What common complication happens when pieces of a heart valve growth break off and travel in the bloodstream?

options.A: Bone fracture
options.B: Kidney stones
options.C: Stroke
options.D: Asthma attack

explanation: When those infected clumps break free, they travel through blood vessels and can block blood flow to the brain, leading to a stroke. Spotting this early saves lives! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h7)

question: How does heavy alcohol use lead to a lack of thiamine?

options.A: By speeding up kidney filtration so the vitamin is quickly sweated out
options.B: By neutralizing stomach acid so that protein digestion stops entirely
options.C: By destroying stored body fat where the vitamin is primarily stored
options.D: By interfering with intestinal absorption and liver storage of the vitamin

explanation: Alcohol irritates the gut lining and stresses the liver, making it impossible for the body to properly take in and hold onto vitamin B1 from food. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h4)

question: During a CT scan with contrast, a patient suddenly develops widespread hives, facial swelling, and mild wheezing. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Ask the patient to hold their breath until the scanning is finished.
options.B: Stop the contrast injection and notify the medical team immediately.
options.C: Reassure the patient that hives are a completely normal side effect.
options.D: Administer a dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient.

explanation: Hives and wheezing indicate an allergic reaction to the contrast media, requiring the immediate cessation of the infusion and prompt emergency medical intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which part of your hand should you use to massage a patient's scalp during a shampoo?

options.A: Knuckles
options.B: Palms of the hands
options.C: Tips of the fingernails
options.D: Pads of the fingers

explanation: Always use the pads of your fingers! It cleans effectively while keeping your fingernails from scratching the patient's sensitive scalp. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why does effective planning help reduce chaos on a hospital ward?

options.A: By eliminating all unexpected medical admissions to the facility
options.B: By allowing nurses to ignore hospital policies during emergencies
options.C: By anticipating patient needs and mapping out required resources ahead of time
options.D: By transferring all administrative duties directly to junior student nurses

explanation: Looking ahead allows managers to prepare staff and supplies before a crisis hits, keeping the ward calm and orderly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of a conceptual framework in a nursing research study?

options.A: To provide a summary of the hospital budget
options.B: To calculate statistical data automatically
options.C: To act as a structural map connecting research ideas
options.D: To list the names of all study participants

explanation: Think of a conceptual framework as your research roadmap! It shows how your main ideas and concepts link together to guide your study smoothly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h1)

question: What are the two major branches of our immune system?

options.A: Active and passive immunity
options.B: Innate and adaptive immunity
options.C: Primary and secondary immunity
options.D: Cellular and humoral immunity

explanation: Great job! The body's defense is split into innate immunity (the fast, general guard) and adaptive immunity (the specialized, long-term force). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is healthcare different from buying regular goods at the market?

options.A: Illness is unpredictable and human survival is at stake
options.B: Hospitals never face constraints on equipment or staffing
options.C: Medical services are always provided free of charge by the state
options.D: Patients always know exactly what medical treatment they require

explanation: Spot on! You can plan when to buy shoes, but sickness catches you off guard. Because lives are on the line, healthcare doesn't follow normal business rules. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of an environmental reservoir of infection?

options.A: A healthcare worker with a mild cold
options.B: An asymptomatic human carrier
options.C: A stray dog carrying the rabies virus
options.D: Contaminated soil and water supplies

explanation: Things around us like soil, water, and food are non-living environmental sources where certain germs love to hide and grow. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical audit in a hospital?

options.A: Comparing current nursing practice against established standards
options.B: Counting the number of visitors on a ward
options.C: Calculating the monthly salary of nursing staff
options.D: Checking the expiration dates of food in the canteen

explanation: A clinical audit is simply checking our actual bedside practice against the golden standard of care to see how well we are doing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which sign tells you an eye infection is likely bacterial rather than viral?

options.A: Clear, watery fluid production
options.B: Severe itching in both eyes
options.C: Complete loss of central vision
options.D: Thick, pus-like eye discharge

explanation: Bacterial eye infections love to produce thick, sticky pus (purulent drainage) that often glues the eyelids shut while sleeping. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main goal of sensory transduction?

options.A: Contracting nearby skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes into the bloodstream
options.C: Converting environmental stimuli into electrical signals
options.D: Storing memories within the cerebral cortex

explanation: You nailed it! Transduction is simply the nervous system's translator, turning physical sensations like touch or light into electrical language the brain can understand. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h4)

question: A nurse tells a patient with diarrhea to wash their hands well after using the toilet. Which part of the chain of infection is this stopping?

options.A: Susceptible host
options.B: Mode of transmission
options.C: Reservoir
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: You're doing great! Handwashing washes germs away, stopping them from traveling to new surfaces or other people through contact. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h3)

question: Which component of hospital waste poses the biggest biological danger to patients and staff?

options.A: Inert plastic polymers
options.B: Pathogenic microorganisms
options.C: Expired dry medications
options.D: Clean paper packaging

explanation: You've got this! Bacteria, viruses, and other germs hiding in body fluids and waste are the main culprits behind biological risks in any healthcare setting. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when planning an IEC campaign?

options.A: Purchase expensive radio airtime for daily health broadcasts
options.B: Design colorful posters and print thousands of information leaflets
options.C: Organize a large community party with local musicians
options.D: Conduct a needs assessment to identify the actual problems of the community

explanation: Planning must always start with assessing the real needs and priorities of the community rather than guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: What is the main driving force behind a non-governmental organization (NGO)?

options.A: Public service and humanitarian relief
options.B: Selling pharmaceuticals to clinics
options.C: Running political campaigns for office
options.D: Generating high profits for owners

explanation: Exactly! NGOs exist to help people and serve communities out of goodwill, not to make money. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community health assessment?

options.A: To gather data on population health needs and available resources
options.B: To close down clinics that do not meet modern standards
options.C: To prescribe individual drugs to every household member
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor sanitation practices

explanation: Spot on! Before a nurse can help a community, they must first find out what problems exist and what resources are already available. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T1#GNS225_U1_T1_h6)

question: A patient waiting for a fasting blood sugar test looks pale, shaky, and dizzy. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask the lab tech to draw their blood right now
options.B: Give them a cup of hot black coffee with sugar
options.C: Check their blood sugar level immediately for low blood sugar
options.D: Tell them to keep waiting patiently for their turn

explanation: Safety first! Shaking, dizziness, and paleness during a fast are classic signs of hypoglycemia. Assess their blood sugar right away before doing anything else. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)

question: What does a nurse typically see during an otoscopic exam of a patient with acute ear infection (otitis media)?

options.A: A clear, translucent eardrum with a sharp cone of light
options.B: A dark perforated hole with dry flaky skin inside the canal
options.C: A bulging, bright red tympanic membrane with obscured landmarks
options.D: A completely pale, flat membrane with prominent bone outlines

explanation: When pus builds up behind the eardrum from an infection, it pushes the drum outward and turns it very red, hiding the normal landmarks. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of these actions goes against basic computer safety rules in the ward?

options.A: Sharing your personal computer login password with a fellow nurse
options.B: Using a barcode scanner to verify a patient's medication before administration
options.C: Reporting a lagging computer screen to the hospital IT help desk
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record system when leaving for lunch

explanation: Never share your password! Whatever is charted under your login account is 100% your professional responsibility. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is recording baseline vital signs and functional ability on the initial assessment sheet important?

options.A: It proves to the family that the nurse arrived on time
options.B: It provides a starting point to measure future clinical progress or decline
options.C: It allows the nurse to discharge the client immediately on day one
options.D: It satisfies administrative paperwork without affecting daily nursing care

explanation: Baseline data gives the nurse a clear point of comparison to see if treatments are working or if the client's health is worsening. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main difference between common cause variation and special cause variation?

options.A: Common cause requires a query, while special cause can be completely ignored.
options.B: Common cause is fully preventable, while special cause is impossible to track.
options.C: Common cause only happens at night, while special cause happens in the morning.
options.D: Common cause is expected and normal, while special cause comes from unusual, unexpected events.

explanation: Common causes are the everyday bumps in the road, while special causes are rare, unexpected surprises that need a closer look. [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h3)

question: When a nursing manager has to settle a dispute between two departments, what should be their main goal?

options.A: Collaborative problem-solving and patient safety
options.B: Ignoring the issue until it resolves on its own
options.C: Punishing the staff members who started the argument
options.D: Closing one of the departments involved

explanation: Spot on! Good leaders look for the root cause and solve problems together, always keeping patient safety at the heart of it all. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why should standard cloth or fabric tailors' tapes be avoided in clinical practice?

options.A: They only measure in inches rather than centimeters
options.B: They are too expensive for community clinics
options.C: They stretch over time and give false readings
options.D: They dissolve easily when exposed to skin moisture

explanation: Fabric stretches with repeated pulling, which ruins the accuracy required for precise health tracking. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why do scientists make semi-synthetic versions of natural antibiotics like penicillin?

options.A: To make the manufacturing process significantly slower and more expensive
options.B: To ensure the drug cannot be absorbed by human gastrointestinal tissue
options.C: To improve stability against stomach acid and broaden antibacterial effectiveness
options.D: To completely remove any chemical similarity to the original fungi

explanation: Tweaking natural penicillin in the lab helps it survive stomach acid and fight off a wider range of stubborn bacteria. Brilliant science! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h4)

question: In the quick AVPU neurological check scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Venous pressure
options.B: Verbal response
options.C: Visual acuity
options.D: Ventilation rate

explanation: You got it! V stands for verbal—meaning the patient reacts or speaks when you talk to them. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why do we only use glutaraldehyde on medical equipment instead of human skin?

options.A: It turns the skin bright yellow for several weeks.
options.B: It is a high-level disinfectant that releases toxic fumes and irritates skin.
options.C: It instantly evaporates when it touches human skin.
options.D: It only works when it is mixed with hot boiling water.

explanation: That's right! Glutaraldehyde is extremely harsh and gives off strong fumes, so it belongs in soaking tanks for instruments, never on a patient's skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h3)

question: How does metabolic stress differ from simple starvation?

options.A: Metabolic stress lowers the heart rate to save body nutrients.
options.B: Metabolic stress forces high energy use while blocking normal tissue conservation.
options.C: Simple starvation causes sudden swelling all over the body.
options.D: Simple starvation causes a faster breakdown of muscle than major trauma.

explanation: While simple starvation triggers energy-saving mechanisms, inflammatory metabolic stress forces continuous tissue breakdown without letting the body conserve resources. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Maternal and Child Health (MCH) services?

options.A: To provide free surgical procedures for aging populations
options.B: To reduce preventable illness and death in mothers and children
options.C: To manage chronic diseases in older adults
options.D: To replace traditional birth practices completely

explanation: You got this! MCH services are specially designed to protect and support the health and survival of mothers and young children. Every win starts with knowing your core goal! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h1)

question: What is the main goal of building a safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Punishing staff members who make medication errors
options.B: Reducing hospital operational costs at all times
options.C: Prioritizing patient safety and shared accountability
options.D: Increasing the speed of patient discharge procedures

explanation: Great job thinking about patient care! A true safety culture means everyone works together to protect patients and shares responsibility, rather than pointing fingers when mistakes happen. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h1)

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter "S" stand for?

options.A: Symptoms
options.B: Solution
options.C: Situation
options.D: Safety

explanation: Easy peasy! SBAR starts with Situation, followed by Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. It keeps our handover chats crisp and clear! [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h5)

question: What should you do immediately when a pregnant woman starts having an eclamptic seizure?

options.A: Hold her arms and legs tightly straight to stop the shaking
options.B: Force a wooden spatula between her teeth to hold the airway open
options.C: Leave the room quickly to call for an ambulance doctor
options.D: Turn her onto her side and protect her from physical injury

explanation: Placing her in the recovery position keeps her airway clear and safe from choking. Never force anything into her mouth! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h4)

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

options.A: The peritoneal membrane inside the abdominal cavity
options.B: The inner lining of the urinary bladder walls
options.C: The basement membrane of the remaining renal tubules
options.D: The semipermeable filter inside the hemodialysis machine

explanation: Peritoneal dialysis is clever! It uses the patient's own rich network of blood vessels inside the abdominal lining (the peritoneum) to filter out waste and extra water. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h6)

question: What happens when a patient takes an anticonvulsant that induces liver enzymes along with their oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: The liver stops processing all medications completely for 24 hours
options.B: The birth control pills are broken down faster, reducing their effectiveness
options.C: The anticonvulsant stops working and breakthrough seizures occur instantly
options.D: The contraceptive hormones build up in the blood to toxic levels

explanation: Certain seizure meds rev up the liver's metabolism like a sports car. This means oral contraceptives get broken down and cleared out way too fast, putting the patient at risk of an unplanned pregnancy. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h6)

question: During an exam, why do clinicians sometimes add potassium hydroxide (KOH) to a vaginal discharge sample?

options.A: To release a fishy odor in bacterial vaginosis
options.B: To lower the sample pH to an acidic level
options.C: To freeze the sample for laboratory transport
options.D: To stain the lactobacilli bacteria bright blue

explanation: It's called the 'whiff test'! Potassium hydroxide helps release those hidden smelly amines, making a fishy odor much easier to spot if BV is present. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of environmental sanitation in public health?

options.A: Controlling environmental factors that harm human health
options.B: Increasing the industrial output of water treatment plants
options.C: Eliminating all insects from urban residential areas
options.D: Reducing the cost of community healthcare delivery

explanation: You've got this! Environmental sanitation simply means managing our surroundings so they don't make us sick. It's all about keeping our communities safe and healthy. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h1)

question: Where are primary immune cells like lymphocytes born and trained?

options.A: Kidneys and pancreas
options.B: Spleen and lymph nodes
options.C: Bone marrow and thymus
options.D: Liver and gallbladder

explanation: Think of the bone marrow and thymus as the ultimate training camp and academy where vital immune cells are produced and prepped for duty. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h3)

question: A patient has overdosed on an opioid. Which signs would you expect to see on assessment?

options.A: High fever and dry, flushed skin
options.B: Excessive sweating and muscle twitching
options.C: Pinpoint pupils and slow breathing
options.D: Rapid heart rate and dilated pupils

explanation: You've got this! Opioids slow down the nervous system. That means they make breathing dangerously slow and cause the pupils to shrink down to tiny 'pinpoints'. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h2)

question: A nursing mother refuses to take her sick child to the clinic because the nearest facility is across a flooded river with no bridge. What primary factor is affecting her health behaviour?

options.A: A lack of personal intelligence
options.B: Stubborn defiance against modern medicine
options.C: An allergic reaction to clinic drugs
options.D: Structural and environmental barriers

explanation: This isn't about her willingness—it's a physical hurdle! Bad roads, long distances, and missing bridges are structural and environmental challenges. You're learning to look at the bigger picture in public health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h3)

question: What kind of conflict happens entirely inside your own head?

options.A: Intrapersonal conflict
options.B: Intragroup conflict
options.C: Intergroup conflict
options.D: Interpersonal conflict

explanation: Intrapersonal conflict is that inner battle we all face—like when you're trying to make a tough personal choice or dealing with stress all by yourself. [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the most common symptom for a patient who is missing just one fallopian tube from birth?

options.A: No symptoms at all
options.B: Permanent primary amenorrhea
options.C: Heavy abnormal uterine bleeding
options.D: Severe chronic pelvic pain

explanation: Exactly! Many women with one missing tube live completely normal lives and only find out by accident during medical scans. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h5)

question: What is usually the first imaging test doctors use to find a heart tumour?

options.A: Routine chest X-ray
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Echocardiogram

explanation: An echo uses sound waves to let us safely peek inside the heart chambers. It's quick, painless, and the go-to tool for spotting masses. Brilliant nursing insight! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a great trick to help a mum manage early morning pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Remaining completely fasting until the afternoon hours
options.B: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks before getting out of bed
options.C: Consuming a heavy, high-fat breakfast right away
options.D: Drinking a large cup of cold whole milk immediately upon waking

explanation: Such a classic nursing tip! A dry biscuit before standing up keeps blood sugar stable and calms that empty, nauseous tummy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h6)

question: What is the best way to greet a client who has missed several family planning appointments?

options.A: Ignore the missed visits and pretend they came on time
options.B: Welcome them warmly and ask gently what made it hard to return
options.C: Report them to the local authorities for breaking rules
options.D: Demand an immediate written apology for wasting clinic time

explanation: Starting with warmth and empathy builds trust, making the client comfortable enough to share the real obstacles they faced. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of 'socialization' within any community?

options.A: Building roads and bridges for commercial transport vehicles
options.B: Collecting taxes to fund government healthcare projects
options.C: Isolating sick patients from healthy members of the public
options.D: Passing down cultural beliefs, rules, and values to new members

explanation: Well done! Socialization is how we learn our society's customs, values, and traditions from generation to generation. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the highest number of skin patches a patient can have to be classified as having paucibacillary leprosy?

options.A: 2 patches
options.B: 20 patches
options.C: 5 patches
options.D: 10 patches

explanation: Paucibacillary simply means 'few bacteria.' Clinically, it's marked by having between one and five skin patches. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h3)

question: What nasty surprise can happen when a patient stays on broad-spectrum antibiotics for too long?

options.A: Total failure of pancreatic enzyme production
options.B: Immediate drop in visual acuity
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of taste
options.D: Superinfection from drug-resistant opportunistic organisms

explanation: When you wipe out good flora, opportunistic bugs like fungi or *C. diff* take over and cause a superinfection. Good to keep in mind for clinicals! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h4)

question: How is the median line on a run chart correctly defined?

options.A: The mathematical average of all plotted values combined
options.B: The absolute highest peak recorded on the graph
options.C: The target goal set by hospital management
options.D: The middle value that divides the data points in half

explanation: The median splits the data so that approximately half of the plotted points sit above it and half sit below it. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which alternative exit route for drugs is especially important for nurses to remember when caring for breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: Mammary excretion
options.B: Sweat gland secretion
options.C: Salivary elimination
options.D: Pulmonary excretion

explanation: Drugs can pass into breast milk through the mammary glands. As nurses, we always check if a mother's medications are safe for her breastfeeding infant! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h5)

question: What do we mean by 'special cause variation' in healthcare?

options.A: The natural healing rate differences among surgical patients
options.B: Unusual events caused by specific, identifiable factors
options.C: The normal daily fluctuation seen in stable hospital units
options.D: Minor differences in how individual nurses fold bed linens

explanation: Great thinking! Special cause variation simply points to a specific trigger or unusual event that disrupts our normal everyday routine. [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a daily operational duty in a running health clinic?

options.A: Designing new national health policies in the capital city
options.B: Maintaining proper cold-chain storage for vaccines and supplies
options.C: Conducting the final statistical evaluation of the program
options.D: Securing international grants for future research studies

explanation: Day-to-day operations involve practical care, like making sure vaccines stay cold and clinic traffic flows smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h5)

question: Why don't diaphragms and cervical caps protect very well against skin-to-skin STIs like HPV?

options.A: They leave the vaginal walls and external skin exposed
options.B: They allow semen to leak freely around the sides of the device
options.C: They dissolve too quickly when exposed to bodily fluids
options.D: They absorb viral particles and push them directly into the uterus

question: What is the main benefit of using Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) when trying to quit?

options.A: It delivers controlled nicotine doses without toxic tar and carbon monoxide
options.B: It permanently repairs lung tissue damage overnight
options.C: It numbs the throat so the patient can never taste tobacco again
options.D: It immediately cures psychological depression

explanation: NRT gives clean nicotine to ease withdrawal without exposing the body to the dangerous toxins found in cigarette smoke. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h7)

question: A patient tells you, 'There's no point in continuing treatment, nothing will ever get better.' As a nurse, how should you take this?

options.A: As a serious indicator of emotional distress requiring immediate attention
options.B: As a sign that the patient wants a different meal tray
options.C: As a funny joke meant to lighten the mood in the ward
options.D: As a normal sign that the patient is recovering fast

explanation: Talk of hopelessness is a critical warning sign. Always take statements like this seriously and report or intervene right away. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h6)

question: What are the specialized sensory receptor cells in the organ of Corti that detect sound called?

options.A: Ossicle cells
options.B: Perilymph cells
options.C: Ganglion cells
options.D: Hair cells

question: A nurse wants to make sure new health posters are clear before printing thousands of copies. What should she do?

options.A: Ask doctors in the capital city to review the picture quality
options.B: Distribute all the posters immediately to save transport costs
options.C: Pre-test the posters with a small group of local community members
options.D: Translate the medical text into Latin for a more professional look

explanation: Brilliant! Always pre-test your materials with the target audience first to catch confusing pictures or messages before mass printing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)

question: A young football player just finished a tough 90-minute match. What kind of snack is best for quick recovery?

options.A: A mix of carbohydrates and protein
options.B: Only pure fat sources like butter
options.C: A heavy meal high in saturated fat
options.D: Plain carbonated water with no nutrients

explanation: Spot on! Carbs quickly refill empty energy tanks, while protein helps repair tired muscles after a heavy game. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h5)

question: Why should nursing educators pay attention to environmental factors?

options.A: It helps them design learning spaces that reduce barriers and support success

options.C: It guarantees that every student will pass their board exams on the first try
options.D: It allows them to grade clinical paperwork much faster

explanation: When lecturers recognize outside influences, they can adjust the learning space to help you overcome hurdles and thrive. Great job thinking like a future nurse educator! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h1)

question: What usually happens during data analysis if a research study completely lacks a theoretical framework?

options.C: The results may be difficult to interpret within a broader scientific context
options.D: The statistical software will automatically generate a new theory

question: Which part of the male urethra is the widest and passes straight through the prostate gland?

question: How does keeping track of a patient's starting diet help the healthcare team?

options.A: It measures if nutrition interventions are working over time

options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory blood investigations

explanation: Spot on! Having a clear starting point lets you track progress and see if your nutrition plan is actually helping the patient get better. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h2)

question: How do hospital policies directly help keep patients safe?

options.A: By ensuring that patients pay their hospital bills on time

options.D: By embedding evidence-based best practices into daily routines

explanation: Policies translate proven safety research into practical, everyday steps that protect our patients from harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h8)

question: Why must management issue a query and hear a nurse's defense before taking disciplinary action?

options.C: To delay disciplinary actions so that the offender can retire voluntarily
options.D: To allow the nurse to immediately apply for employment in another sector

question: Why do we need to separate microorganisms from a mixed environment before studying them?

options.C: Microbes cannot survive unless they are grown entirely by themselves
options.D: Mixed populations always destroy their own growth media instantly

question: What is one of the most important rules for giving high-quality chest compressions during CPR?

question: A patient eats a very salty meal. What is their body most likely to do right after?

options.B: Thirst increases and the kidneys retain more water
options.C: The kidneys immediately excrete all circulating sodium
options.D: Blood pressure drops rapidly due to sudden dehydration

question: How do you acquire knowledge through the empirical method?

options.B: Through pure logical thought without looking at the patient
options.C: By accepting traditional beliefs without testing
options.D: By waiting for a sudden gut feeling or intuition

explanation: Empiricism means gathering facts using your own senses—like looking at a wound, touching a pulse, or listening to lung sounds. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the biggest downside to using benzodiazepines over a long period?

options.C: They permanently destroy brain neurotransmitters.
options.D: They take at least six weeks to start working.

question: What is the statistical word for the value that shows up most often in a set of data?

question: Which of these does NOT belong in a study's methodology section?

explanation: Methodology sticks strictly to the facts of how the study was done. Personal thoughts and opinions wait for the discussion part! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h4)

question: How do automated hospital beds make a nurse's duty easier?

options.B: By completely replacing the need for bedside nursing assistants
options.C: By making regular patient safety rounds completely unnecessary
options.D: By reducing physical strain during patient repositioning and transfers

question: What is the leading cause of severe trauma and head injuries on our roads here in Nigeria?

question: Why should families pick a specific meeting place outside their home when planning for emergencies?

options.C: To serve as a temporary community clinic

question: Which objective of health education deals with building practical self-care skills like handwashing?

options.A: Cognitive objective
options.B: Affective objective

options.D: Administrative objective

question: During a massive flood, what is the primary role of security agencies like the police?

options.A: Crowd control, maintenance of law and order, and safe corridors
options.B: Designing permanent structural housing for displaced families
options.C: Clinical triage and emergency surgical interventions at the bedside
options.D: Purchasing medical equipment and pharmaceutical drugs from abroad

explanation: Police and civil defense keep people safe, manage crowds, and clear paths so medical teams can get through. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T8#GNS315_U5_T8_h3)

question: A breastfeeding mother who delivered six weeks ago asks for a contraceptive implant. What should you tell her?

options.A: She must first undergo a liver biopsy to prove her body can tolerate the progestin hormone
options.B: She is completely ineligible because implants will immediately dry up her breast milk supply
options.C: She is eligible, as progestin-only implants do not interfere with milk production and are safe during breastfeeding
options.D: She must wait until her baby is at least one year old before any hormonal method can be discussed

question: What is the main purpose of MeSH terms in healthcare databases?

options.C: To automatically generate nursing care plans for patients
options.D: To translate clinical articles into multiple foreign languages

explanation: MeSH terms standardize medical concepts so that synonyms and different writing styles do not hide relevant articles from your search. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h5)

question: What does interdependence mean within a healthcare system?

options.A: Every hospital department operates completely on its own
options.B: A change or delay in one part directly affects other parts
options.C: Financial profit is shared equally among all workers
options.D: Only doctors have an impact on overall patient recovery

explanation: Interdependence means elements rely on each other, so a failure or slowdown in one area ripples through the rest of the system. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is a common outcome of poor communication between intimate partners?

options.B: Complete elimination of sexual dysfunction

options.D: Performance pressure and emotional withdrawal

question: Maternal education in Nigeria is most closely linked to which of these health outcomes?

options.A: Cost of private health insurance
options.B: Frequency of major surgical operations
options.C: Availability of hospital bed spaces
options.D: Child immunization and nutrition rates

question: What does plagiarism mean?

options.D: Using a medical dictionary to look up a new word

question: Why do maternity homes hold clinical audits and review close-calls?

options.C: To identify safety gaps and improve future clinical care quality
options.D: To reduce the number of patients seeking care at the facility

question: A lab report shows a patient's sputum sample has acid-fast bacilli. Which disease are doctors likely checking for?

question: Why are faith-based health clinics so important in many Nigerian communities?

options.D: They focus exclusively on urban corporate executives

question: Why do older adults generally need fewer calories each day compared to younger adults?

options.C: They store all their energy directly as water weight

question: What is the primary viral cause of severe, dehydrating diarrhea in infants and young children?

question: Where do water-soluble peptide hormones usually find their target cell receptors?

question: Why is it clinically important for nurses to separate biological sex from gender?

question: What is the primary purpose of nursing research?

question: Why does a repeat infection with the same virus trigger a much faster immune response?

question: Which body measurement is most commonly used in the community to quickly screen young children for severe malnutrition?

question: How does deep-seated gender inequality contribute to the persistence of child marriage?
