options.C: It devalues girls' education and autonomy compared to boys
options.D: It forces boys to leave school earlier than girls

explanation: When communities view girls only through the lens of domestic and reproductive duties, keeping them in school or allowing them to choose a career is discouraged. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why are nurses such valuable members of a quality improvement team?

options.A: They write hospital policy manuals alone
options.B: They have formal training in hospital finance
options.C: They make all final administrative decisions
options.D: They spend the most time at the bedside

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses are right there with patients every day, they see firsthand what works and where things go wrong in clinical care. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h1)

question: How does a prospective study differ fundamentally from a retrospective study?

options.A: Prospective studies look forward at future events, while retrospective studies look backward at past records
options.B: Prospective studies involve no data collection, while retrospective studies involve heavy data collection
options.C: Prospective studies are always qualitative, while retrospective studies are always quantitative
options.D: Prospective studies use animal subjects, while retrospective studies only use human patients

explanation: The core difference lies in the temporal orientation, with prospective starting in the present and moving forward, and retrospective starting in the present and looking backward. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal challenge faced by public health institutions?

options.A: Excessive financial profits and private wealth accumulation
options.B: Bureaucratic delays in procuring medical supplies
options.C: Brain drain of experienced healthcare workers
options.D: Infrastructure decay and power supply failures

explanation: You nailed it! Public hospitals rarely swim in extra cash or private wealth; rather, they usually struggle with underfunding and resource shortages. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h5)

question: How do traditional community norms help keep early teenage marriage going?

options.A: By banning young women from working outside the home until they wed
options.B: By legally requiring all citizens to marry before completing secondary school
options.C: By viewing early marriage as a traditional marker of female honor and maturity
options.D: By offering free medical care exclusively to married teenage girls

explanation: Culture often links early marriage with family honor and good character, putting strong pressure on families to follow tradition. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the name of the age-related muscle loss condition that often affects nutritional assessments in older adults?

options.A: Sarcopenia
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Atherosclerosis
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Well done! Sarcopenia is the gradual, natural decrease in muscle mass and strength as people age, which changes what normal body composition looks like for them. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common bottleneck when trying to control government health spending?

options.A: Bureaucratic inefficiency and delayed fund releases
options.B: Weak accounting systems leading to resource leakage
options.C: Immediate and transparent tracking of every kobo at the clinic level
options.D: Political interference in siting capital projects

explanation: Real-time tracking of every kobo is the ideal goal we want to achieve, not a bottleneck. Weak accounting and delays are the actual problems! [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why have state governments in Nigeria introduced State Health Insurance Agencies alongside the federal scheme?

options.A: To stop international donors from funding local health programs
options.B: To reach informal sector workers and rural residents more effectively
options.C: To completely replace all federal public hospitals with private clinics
options.D: To ensure that healthcare services are exclusively funded by taxes

explanation: State schemes help capture local traders, artisans, and rural dwellers who are often missed by federal formal-sector plans. Great thinking! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h4)

question: When does bereavement support typically begin and end in a hospice program?

options.A: It begins only after one full year has passed
options.B: It continues for months after the patient passes away
options.C: It only occurs during the final week of the patient's life
options.D: It stops immediately the moment the patient dies

explanation: Bereavement care is an ongoing service that supports grieving family members for many months following their loss. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: How do efflux pumps help resistant bacteria survive?

options.A: They alter the outer cell membrane to block drug entry completely
options.B: They rapidly push incoming drug molecules out of the cell
options.C: They break down antibiotics using specialized enzyme proteins
options.D: They manufacture protective spores during periods of starvation

explanation: You can picture efflux pumps like tiny bouncers at a club door—they quickly throw the drug right back out before it can cause any trouble inside the cell! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h2)

question: What does a risk assessment mainly look at?

options.A: The speed at which emergency vehicles can travel
options.B: The exact budget needed to rebuild a damaged clinic
options.C: The likelihood of a hazard and population vulnerability
options.D: The personal medical history of disaster survivors

explanation: Spot on! Risk assessment combines how likely an event is with how exposed and vulnerable the people are. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which processing method destroys all microorganisms, including bacterial spores?

options.A: Cleaning
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sanitization

explanation: Sterilization is the only process that completely eliminates every form of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial spores. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why are maternity homes so important in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They replace federal tertiary teaching hospitals completely
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medications during labor
options.C: They offer free surgical care funded by international donors
options.D: They serve as local bridges to care when distant hospitals are hard to reach

explanation: Spot on! By being close by, they bridge the gap so mums don't have to travel huge distances just to get basic care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h1)

question: What does the 'R' stand for in the START triage system used during disasters?

options.A: Rapid
options.B: Resuscitation
options.C: Recovery
options.D: Respiratory

explanation: START stands for Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment, designed for fast categorization in mass casualty incidents. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why might a patient with severe carbon monoxide poisoning show a falsely normal or high oxygen saturation reading on a pulse oximeter?

options.A: Carbon monoxide makes the pulse rate extremely fast
options.B: Cold fingers stop the machine from recording low numbers
options.C: Bright lights in the room interfere with the infrared sensors
options.D: The device reads carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin just like oxygen

explanation: Standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between oxygen and carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin, leading to dangerously misleading high readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why are community health nurses often the first to spot developmental delays in children?

options.A: They perform all surgical procedures in the country
options.B: They interact with families regularly during home and clinic visits
options.C: They manage the national legal courts
options.D: They live in federal legislative offices

explanation: Because community health nurses visit homes and local clinics often, they are in the best position to notice early developmental milestones and red flags. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T7#GNS225_U5_T7_h5)

question: How should you handle your personal moral beliefs when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Refuse to provide any medication or comfort
options.B: Put personal views aside to deliver respectful care
options.C: Report the client to religious leaders
options.D: Argue with the client about their life choices

explanation: Professional nursing ethics mean we always put our patient's health and dignity first, delivering unbiased, compassionate care no matter our personal background. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: Which action shows that a nurse is truly practicing active listening?

options.A: Giving full attention and minimizing distractions
options.B: Interrupting to offer quick medical solutions
options.C: Looking around the room for the next client
options.D: Writing in a chart while the patient speaks

explanation: Active listening means putting other tasks aside and showing the patient they have your complete, caring focus. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h6)

question: What usually happens to ordinary families when they have to pay heavy out-of-pocket costs for healthcare?

options.A: Guaranteed reimbursement of medical bills by local governments
options.B: Catastrophic health expenditures that drain household savings
options.C: Automatic enrollment in free federal health insurance schemes
options.D: Immediate access to advanced surgical care in private hospitals

explanation: When you have to pay straight from your pocket without insurance, sudden illnesses can easily wipe out a family's savings and drag them into severe poverty. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h1)

question: Where does a non-competitive antagonist usually bind on a cell receptor?

options.A: Directly inside the active agonist binding groove
options.B: Freely inside the fluid portion of the blood plasma
options.C: On the outer nuclear membrane of the cell
options.D: At an allosteric site away from the active spot

explanation: Instead of fighting for the main entrance, a non-competitive antagonist sneaks around to a side entrance (allosteric site) and changes the whole shape of the receptor. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T7#GNS125_U5_T7_h3)

question: A Nigerian ward lacks high-tech digital safety alerts. What can nurses do right now to keep patients safe?

options.A: Keep all incident logs hidden from hospital management
options.B: Refuse to admit new patients until digital systems arrive
options.C: Rely entirely on patient memory for medication administration
options.D: Use rigorous verbal cross-checks and thorough bedside handovers with colleagues

explanation: Well done! Simple teamwork habits like good verbal handovers and checking each other's work go a long way without needing expensive computers. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is an important nursing duty after putting mydriatic eye drops in a patient's eyes for an exam?

options.A: Flush both eyes right away with normal saline
options.B: Keep them locked in a dark room for a whole day
options.C: Warn them about blurry vision and bright light sensitivity
options.D: Check their blood pressure every five minutes

explanation: Mydriatic drops widen the pupil and relax focusing muscles, making bright lights uncomfortable and vision blurry for a few hours. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is promoting local Nigerian foods better than relying on foreign supplements for community health?

options.A: Local foods have zero carbohydrates and eliminate all diseases
options.B: Local foods are affordable, culturally acceptable, and readily available
options.C: Local foods never spoil even without refrigeration
options.D: Imported supplements are always illegal to prescribe in clinics

explanation: Using familiar, accessible foodstuffs empowers families to eat well long-term without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h8)

question: What is a simple, practical way to store extra green vegetables when electricity is unreliable?

options.A: Sealing in airtight glass jars with heavy salt
options.B: Soaking them continuously in vinegar
options.C: Sun-drying or blanching
options.D: Deep-freezing for three years

explanation: Correct! Sun-drying and blanching are time-tested ways to keep your veggies from spoiling without needing a fridge. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h6)

question: You feel the uterus and it is soft and boggy right after delivery. What is your very first action?

options.A: Apply warm compresses to the lower back
options.B: Administer oral pain relief medication
options.C: Transfer the patient to a tertiary hospital immediately
options.D: Perform immediate fundal uterine massage

explanation: Massage helps the uterine muscles tighten up and clamp down on bleeding vessels. It's a quick, lifesaving first step! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is your very first action if a surgical drain accidentally falls completely out of a patient's wound?

options.A: Try to gently push the same tube right back into the hole
options.B: Leave the open wound uncovered so fresh air can dry it out
options.C: Cover the open site with a sterile dressing and notify the doctor
options.D: Wash the fallen tube with soap and tape it back onto the skin

explanation: Never try to push a fallen drain back in—that introduces germs! Instead, cover the site with a sterile dressing right away and call the doctor. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)

question: What is the main role of the thymus gland in the human body?

options.A: Regulating blood sugar levels after meals
options.B: Producing bile to help digest dietary fats
options.C: Maturing T-lymphocytes for the immune system
options.D: Filtering bacteria out of swallowed food

explanation: Immature white blood cells travel to the thymus where they develop into functional T-cells capable of fighting infection. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is a major health benefit of using traditional, unrefined red palm oil in moderate amounts?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for protein in the diet
options.B: It is naturally rich in beta-carotene and beneficial antioxidants
options.C: It has zero calories and prevents weight gain
options.D: It contains only trans fats that clear out blocked arteries

explanation: Unrefined red palm oil keeps its natural plant nutrients, like carotenoids, giving it that rich color and healthy antioxidant boost. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h4)

question: What is a major effect of severe heatstroke on the body's cells?

options.A: Disruption of vital enzymatic reactions and cellular function
options.B: Complete cessation of electrical activity in the skeletal muscles
options.C: Rapid production of large quantities of protective body fat
options.D: Permanent freezing of blood vessels in the upper extremities

explanation: Extreme heat scrambles the delicate proteins and enzymes our cells need to work. Cooling the patient down quickly is a true medical emergency priority! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: A patient treated for a wasp sting allergy feels fine after 30 minutes and wants to go home. What should you tell them?

options.A: Explain that the patient must stay longer because a secondary reaction can happen hours later
options.B: Tell the patient that once symptoms stop, they will never have another reaction
options.C: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to be completely safe before leaving
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines

explanation: Allergic reactions can strike twice! We call this a biphasic reaction, meaning the patient needs to stick around for observation just in case symptoms return hours later. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: Why is writing your notes down promptly in the shared health record so important?

options.A: It allows family members to edit the medical diagnosis
options.B: It eliminates the need for nurses to visit the home
options.C: It prevents conflicting instructions among different team members
options.D: It guarantees that therapy sessions will last longer

explanation: Since different team members visit at different times, clear shared notes ensure everyone is on the same page regarding the patient's care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when caring for a patient with a known severe drug allergy?

options.A: Telling the patient they can safely take a tiny dose of the drug again
options.B: Putting clear allergy alerts in the patient chart
options.C: Notifying the hospital pharmacy about the allergy
options.D: Educating the family on how to avoid the drug

explanation: Never give a drug again if a patient has a true severe allergy! They must avoid it completely for life. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h8)

question: How did healthcare delivery change globally after Primary Health Care was introduced?

options.A: It focused exclusively on building high-tech specialist hospitals in rural areas
options.B: It transferred all health responsibilities away from governments to private individuals
options.C: It eliminated traditional medicine entirely in favor of imported pharmaceuticals
options.D: It shifted from expensive hospital-centric curative care to community-based preventive care

explanation: You got it! Before PHC, the system waited for people to fall sick and travel far to hospitals. PHC changed this by bringing prevention and basic care directly to the people. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h1)

question: Where are cytochrome P450 enzymes mostly found in the human body?

options.A: In the kidneys
options.B: In the liver
options.C: In the bone marrow
options.D: In the skeletal muscles

explanation: You nailed it! The liver is packed with cytochrome P450 enzymes, making it the main engine for breaking down drugs in our bodies. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h3)

question: What quick bedside test helps confirm if a skin rash is caused by a fungus?

options.A: Gram stain of blood cultures
options.B: Complete blood cell count
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount

explanation: Spot on! Adding KOH melts away the skin cells while leaving the stubborn fungal threads clearly visible under a microscope. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h5)

question: Why is it helpful for student nurses to understand research paradigms?

options.A: To evaluate published studies and choose proper evidence for care
options.B: To calculate exact medication dosages for surgical patients
options.C: To diagnose rare diseases using laboratory blood test results
options.D: To write hospital administration policies without clinical data

explanation: Knowing this helps you look at a research paper and figure out if the findings make sense and can actually help your patients on the ward. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which drug class works by acting as faulty building blocks that trick the reverse transcriptase enzyme?

options.A: Integrase Inhibitors
options.B: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs)
options.C: Entry Inhibitors
options.D: Protease Inhibitors (PIs)

explanation: Well done! NRTIs send in fake building blocks. The virus gets tricked into using them, which completely halts the creation of its viral DNA. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h3)

question: An older adult patient in the ward feels sad about losing their physical strength and independence. Which core emotional need is most challenged here?

options.A: Unconditional parental caregiving
options.B: Financial asset accumulation
options.C: Dignity and a sense of life fulfillment
options.D: Identity exploration and peer acceptance

explanation: Growing older and losing independence can make patients feel vulnerable. Protecting their dignity and helping them feel valued is a key nursing duty. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h3)

question: When should you close a sharps container and switch it for a new one?

options.A: Only at the end of every calendar month
options.B: When the outside label begins to fade
options.C: When it reaches about three-quarters full
options.D: When it is completely overflowing at the top

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarter mark keeps items from sticking out of the top and poking someone. Safety first! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the simple difference between inter-rater and intra-rater reliability?

options.A: Inter-rater uses computers, while intra-rater relies entirely on patient self-reporting
options.B: Inter-rater measures time, while intra-rater measures physical instrument weight
options.C: Inter-rater looks at agreement between different observers, while intra-rater looks at consistency within a single observer
options.D: There is no real difference, as both terms mean the exact same thing in research

explanation: Remember the prefixes: 'Inter-' means between different people (two nurses comparing notes), while 'intra-' means within the same person grading things over time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h5)

question: What percentage of the annual national budget did the Abuja Declaration recommend for health spending in African countries?

options.A: Exactly 5 percent
options.B: At least 15 percent
options.C: Up to 50 percent
options.D: Not more than 2 percent

explanation: The famous Abuja Declaration set a benchmark of 15 percent for government investment in health. Memorize this one—it's a classic exam favorite! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main chemical trigger in your blood that tells your brain it is time to breathe?

options.A: Nitrogen gas dissolved in plasma
options.B: High levels of blood glucose
options.C: Carbon dioxide levels in the blood
options.D: Oxygen levels in the arterial blood

explanation: You got it! A buildup of carbon dioxide is the strongest alarm bell your body uses to say 'time to take a breath.' [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurses collect a microbiological specimen from a patient?

options.A: To measure the exact white blood cell count in the blood
options.B: To clean out infected tissue from an open wound
options.C: To determine the patient's blood type for transfusion
options.D: To identify the specific microorganism causing an infection

explanation: We collect these samples to find out exactly which germ is making the patient sick, so treatment can hit the right target! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h1)

question: What should you do FIRST when a portable monitor suddenly lets out a loud, urgent alarm?

options.A: Document a cardiac arrest in the patient chart right away
options.B: Immediately silence the device and walk away to find a doctor
options.C: Turn off the monitor power switch to stop the annoying noise
options.D: Assess the patient's physical condition and check the sensor placement

explanation: Patient first, always! Check the patient and make sure the sensor hasn't just popped off before jumping to conclusions. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h5)

question: A doctor orders a wound culture and an IV antibiotic for a new patient. Which order of steps is correct?

options.A: The order of these two actions does not matter clinically
options.B: Collect the wound culture first, then start the antibiotic
options.C: Give half the antibiotic dose, collect the culture, then give the rest
options.D: Administer the antibiotic first, then collect the culture the next day

explanation: Always culture before you treat! If you start the antibiotic first, it might kill the bacteria before the lab can catch it. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which print material is best to hang on a busy clinic waiting room wall to grab quick attention?

options.A: Posters
options.B: Textbooks
options.C: Logbooks
options.D: Brochures

explanation: Posters are large and eye-catching, making them perfect for high-traffic walls where patients can quickly glance at them while waiting. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h2)

question: Why is checking the bladder so important in the first few hours after childbirth?

options.A: Urinary retention always leads to permanent kidney failure
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes heavy bleeding
options.C: Bladder fullness is the primary sign of postpartum preeclampsia
options.D: It prevents the lochia from changing from red to white

explanation: Think of it this way: a full bladder takes up space and pushes against the uterus, stopping it from contracting properly. Keeping the bladder empty keeps mom safe from extra bleeding! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h3)

question: Why do nurses need to speak up and do advocacy work alongside regular bedside care?

options.A: Patients will refuse medications unless nurses also lobby local leaders
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to submit weekly political reports
options.C: Clinical care alone cannot fix underlying systemic gaps causing illness
options.D: Clinical nursing duties do not take up enough of a nurse's work shift

explanation: Great thinking! Treating patients at the bedside is vital, but if bad living conditions or broken policies keep making people sick, we have to advocate for wider changes too. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which strategy is most important when trying to shift a hospital's workplace culture?

options.A: Sending out a single memo explaining the new hospital mission statement
options.B: Threatening disciplinary action for anyone who questions hospital leadership
options.C: Implementing deliberate, sustained actions that embed new values into daily work
options.D: Replacing all senior nursing staff with new graduates from local universities

explanation: Spot on! Changing culture doesn't happen from a single memo; it takes consistent, long-term effort built into everyday ward routines. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h5)

question: How long should a patient rest quietly before having their blood pressure measured?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 5 minutes
options.C: No rest is needed
options.D: At least 1 hour

explanation: A short resting period ensures that recent physical activity or rushing does not falsely elevate the blood pressure reading. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h3)

question: Which stage of dementia usually lasts the longest and is known for noticeable confusion and wandering?

options.A: Pre-clinical stage
options.B: Early stage
options.C: Middle stage
options.D: Late stage

explanation: The middle stage is typically the longest. It brings clear behavioral changes, like wandering and needing help with daily tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why is taking off your PPE in the correct, specific order so important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next shift
options.B: To prevent transferring trapped pathogens from the gear onto your skin
options.C: To prevent the plastic straps from snapping during disposal
options.D: To speed up the process so you can leave the isolation room faster

explanation: The outside of your PPE is covered in germs. If you take it off carelessly, you'll end up wiping those germs right onto your face or hands! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h8)

question: What is the main goal of teaching Kegel exercises to someone with urinary incontinence?

options.A: To strengthen the pelvic floor muscles supporting the bladder
options.B: To relax the abdominal wall during a physical exam
options.C: To stretch the ureters and widen the urinary tract
options.D: To increase total daily urine production in the kidneys

explanation: Kegels tone up those pelvic floor muscles, giving the patient much better control over when they go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h6)

question: What is a major economic barrier that limits a woman's healthcare autonomy?

options.A: Financial dependency on male heads of households
options.B: Too much freedom in spending personal income
options.C: An overabundance of free public health clinics
options.D: Excessive participation in local market associations

explanation: Without personal income or financial control, women often cannot afford transport fare or medical bills without male approval. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h2)

question: Why are newborn babies at a higher risk for drug toxicity?

options.A: An overactive immune system clearing drugs too fast
options.B: Increased stomach acidity destroying oral medications
options.C: Immature liver enzymes and slow kidney filtration
options.D: Too much muscle mass and very high body water

explanation: Babies are precious and delicate! Their organs are still developing, meaning their liver and kidneys cannot process and clear medications as quickly as adult organs do. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is the main shift that occurs during an epidemiological transition?

options.A: A shift from infectious diseases to chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: A shift from high birth rates to zero population growth
options.C: A shift from urban living to rural farming settlements
options.D: A shift from hospital care to traditional healing practices

explanation: As societies develop and life expectancy increases, the primary health burden moves away from acute infections toward chronic lifestyle and age-related illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-leave nursing risk assessment?

options.A: To ensure the patient no longer requires follow-up care
options.B: To collect payment for hospital accommodation
options.C: To evaluate suicide risk, aggression potential, and ensure a clear emergency plan exists
options.D: To check if the patient's personal clothing is clean

explanation: A quick risk check helps nurses spot potential dangers and makes sure everyone has a solid backup plan if things get tough. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: How do modern communities (like online student groups) change our view of physical borders?

options.A: Individuals can no longer feel attached to their neighborhoods
options.B: Physical maps are no longer used by any government agencies
options.C: Geographical borders completely disappear during public health emergencies
options.D: People can form connected groups based on shared interests without living near each other

explanation: Today, technology and social media let people connect and support each other across long distances, stretching beyond just physical location. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h2)

question: How should a nursing team view a test that doesn't show the expected improvement during the Study phase?

options.A: As a valuable learning opportunity to understand what does not work
options.B: As a personal failure of every nurse working on the hospital ward
options.C: As proof that quality improvement projects are completely useless
options.D: As a sign that they should hide the data from the nursing director

explanation: Exactly! In QI, even a failed test teaches us something useful. It brings us one step closer to what actually works. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is teaching sleep hygiene so important in recovery?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nutritional counseling
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never feel tired again
options.C: It helps regulate rest patterns to restore depleted nervous energy
options.D: It cures underlying infectious diseases

explanation: You're doing great! Good sleep habits give the tired nervous system the deep rest it needs to repair itself. Keep practicing daily! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h7)

question: What happens when you cram way too much data into a single research table?

options.A: It changes the fundamental type of the study
options.B: Journals will charge extra money for the paper weight
options.C: It becomes confusing and hard for readers to digest
options.D: It automatically makes all the calculations mathematically incorrect

explanation: Tables are supposed to simplify life, not overwhelm the brain. Too much data in one spot defeats the whole purpose! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h6)

question: When should a nurse researcher pick a qualitative design over a quantitative one?

options.A: When testing if a new medication lowers blood pressure faster
options.B: When exploring the personal meaning and lived experience of a condition
options.C: When measuring the exact hospital readmission rate over a year
options.D: When calculating the average cost of surgical supplies per patient

explanation: Choose qualitative when you want to dive deep into personal stories, coping styles, and human emotions. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is a major socioeconomic challenge that can make storing home medications very difficult?

options.A: Too many professional nursing visits in one week
options.B: Unstable housing or lack of reliable electricity
options.C: An overabundance of municipal transportation options
options.D: Excessive amounts of local community food banks

explanation: Exactly. Think of medications like insulin—without stable electricity or a fridge, keeping them safe at home becomes a huge hurdle. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main reason nurses use hypothesis testing in research?

options.A: To prove that personal clinical opinions are always correct
options.B: To increase the financial cost of operating a hospital ward
options.C: To evaluate if observed data differences are real or due to chance
options.D: To eliminate the need for collecting patient outcome data

explanation: Great job thinking like a researcher! Hypothesis testing simply uses math to check if what we see in a study is a true effect or just random luck. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h1)

question: What is the main difference between an acute care EHR and an ambulatory EHR?

options.A: Acute care systems focus on round-the-clock hospital monitoring, while ambulatory systems track long-term outpatient visits
options.B: Acute care systems prohibit nurses from charting, whereas ambulatory systems are strictly for nursing documentation
options.C: Ambulatory systems can only be accessed inside intensive care units using desktop computers
options.D: Ambulatory systems require minute-by-minute surgical checklists, while acute care systems only track yearly checkups

explanation: Spot on! Acute care is for the hustle and bustle of 24/7 hospital wards, while ambulatory care tracks regular visits at out-patient clinics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why central nervous system neurons struggle to repair themselves?

options.A: Schwann cells create perfect guiding tubes for repair
options.B: Oligodendrocytes fail to form functional repair tracts
options.C: Growth-inhibiting molecules block axonal sprouts
options.D: Astrocytes form physical scar tissue blocks

explanation: Schwann cells actually help nerves heal, but they live in the *peripheral* nervous system, not the central nervous system. The CNS lacks this helpful environment! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h8)

question: What is the first thing you should do when building a histogram from raw numbers?

options.A: Calculate the exact average of the categorical groups
options.B: Find the range by identifying the lowest and highest values
options.C: Color the bars using alternating bright shades
options.D: Draw the vertical and horizontal axes freehand

explanation: You always want to know your lowest and highest numbers first so you know how wide your chart needs to stretch! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h4)

question: Patient, health, environment, and nursing. Why are these four big ideas so special in our field?

options.A: They represent the four core pillars that define nursing practice
options.B: They are required elements for hospital budget planning
options.C: They determine the legal penalties for medical malpractice
options.D: They outline the exact daily schedule for ward nurses

explanation: Spot on! These four concepts make up the 'metaparadigm' of nursing—basically, the big four pillars that every single nursing theory builds upon. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which cells swallow trapped fats inside artery walls to help form fatty streaks?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Macrophages
options.C: Fibroblasts
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Macrophages are our immune cleanup cells, but when they eat too much trapped fat in the arteries, they turn into foam cells and start plaque buildup. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why would a patient who took a severe drug overdose be put on a mechanical ventilator?

options.A: Reversal of central nervous system toxicity
options.B: Immediate elimination of the drug from the lungs
options.C: Airway protection and respiratory support
options.D: Prevention of future drug dependency

explanation: When someone is deeply unconscious from an overdose, their body forgets to protect its own airway. The ventilator keeps them breathing safely and stops any spit or vomit from entering their lungs. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h1)

question: What makes thyroid hormones act a bit differently than other amino acid-derived hormones?

options.A: They are large proteins made of hundreds of linked amino acids
options.B: They only function within the nervous system as fast neurotransmitters
options.C: They cannot travel in the bloodstream without dissolving in red blood cells
options.D: They are fat-soluble and enter cells to bind intracellular receptors

explanation: Even though they start from an amino acid, thyroid hormones behave like fat-loving steroids—they slip right inside the cell to do their work. Tricky, but you'll never forget it now! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h3)
